Introduction

About

I'm an Aerospace Engineering undergraduate at SRMIST, Kattankulathur, interested in the engineering and science behind space exploration.

My interests span space systems, propulsion, orbital mechanics, and the broader physics of the universe. Alongside my engineering education, I pursue scientific research and writing, exploring complex ideas through literature, evidence, and accessible explanations.

Through my technical learning, research contributions, and independent writing, I'm working toward a stronger foundation in aerospace engineering while continuing to explore the questions that make space science fascinating to me.

Hands-on learning

Workshops

Hands-on workshops and programmes, mostly in rocketry and drones, connected to my degree.

Rocketry workshop

From Thrust to Flight: Mastering the Science of Rocket Modelling

26 September 2026 · Overnight workshop · Aaruush '26 · SRMIST, Kattankulathur
Organised by Team Aaruush at SRMIST, with Thrust Tech India. Certificate of Participation.

This rocket modelling workshop offered a closer look at the science and engineering behind rocketry, from the fundamentals of propulsion to the principles that make rocket flight possible.

What made it interesting was connecting concepts from textbooks with their practical applications. The photos show rocket design software, a model rocket, and launches from the workshop. As an Aerospace Engineering undergraduate, it left me more curious about the engineering involved in designing, developing, and launching rockets.

Thank you to Thrust Tech India, Aaruush, and SRMIST for organising the workshop.

Drone workshop

SkyVision 2026: FPV Drone Build and Fly Workshop

2 – 3 September 2026 · 16 hours · SRMIST, Kattankulathur
Organised by the Department of Aerospace Engineering, SRMIST, with the Aerospace Systems Research Laboratory (ASRL). Certificate of Participation.

This was my first drone workshop at SRMIST. Over two days and 16 hours in the Aerospace Hangar, we went from individual components to a functional FPV drone, learning how mechanical systems, electronics, and coding come together to make flight possible.

The part that stayed with me was putting on the FPV goggles, picking up the controller, and seeing the world from the drone's perspective. There is a difference between learning the theory of flight and experiencing it firsthand.

As a first-year Aerospace Engineering student, experiences like this remind me why I chose the field. There is much more to aerospace than what we learn in classrooms, and I am only beginning to explore it.

Technical work

Projects

Completed

RPG Mini Game

A stat-allocation game where players distribute points across Strength, Intelligence, and Charisma to unlock one of three hidden archetypes.

My contribution
Designed and built the game logic, first as a Python command-line tool and later as a Streamlit web app.
Tools and methods
Python and Streamlit. The archetype logic is written as pure functions, separate from the display, with session state handling persistence between reruns.
Outcome
Separating logic from display made the rebuild straightforward. The main lesson was managing state in a framework that reruns the whole script on every interaction.
GitHub profile ↗
Completed

Task Tracker

A command-line task manager that stores tasks with priorities and due dates in a CSV file.

My contribution
Built it to learn file input and output and data persistence in Python directly.
Tools and methods
Python and the csv module. Tasks are read into memory on launch, sorted by priority for display, and written back on every change.
Outcome
Known limitation: rewriting the whole file on each edit does not scale and risks data loss if the program stops mid-write.
GitHub profile ↗
